label: Agents in production
blurb: Getting agents past a demo means being able to say, with evidence, that they will behave on the next hundred million conversations. I work on evaluation harnesses rigorous enough to gate a deployment, and on the failure modes that only appear once real customers are on the other end.
papers: Building Customer Support AI Agents at 100M-User Scale: An Evaluation-Driven Framework
talks: Building Production LLM Agents: An Evaluation-Driven Playbook
SimulationMaxxing: How we ship agents 20× faster

label: Alignment and post-training
blurb: Preference optimization is usually studied through its objective, but the shape of the reward and the robustness of the reward model matter just as much. I look at where the standard recipes are brittle and what to change so alignment holds up outside the benchmark.
papers: AlphaPO: Reward Shape Matters for LLM Alignment
On the Robustness of Reward Models for Language Model Alignment

label: Efficiency at scale
blurb: A model that cannot be served is a result, not a product. This thread covers compressing and distilling large models down to a serving budget, quantizing optimizer state so training fits, and scheduling inference so latency targets survive real traffic.
papers: Scaling Down, Serving Fast: Compressing and Deploying Efficient LLMs for Recommendation Systems
Effective Quantization of Muon Optimizer States
LLM Query Scheduling with Prefix Reuse and Latency Constraints

label: Recommender systems at scale
blurb: I have worked across the recommender stack: retrieval, ranking, personalization, and the large-scale constrained optimization that sits on top of it. That last part meant solving linear programs with trillions of variables.
papers: Practical Design of Performant Recommender Systems using Large-scale Linear Programming-based Global Inference
Efficient Algorithms for Leveraging LLMs for Generative and Predictive Recommender Systems
LiRank: Industrial Large Scale Ranking Models at LinkedIn
